You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data points to late 2014 or early 2015. Unemployment is 5.9%, which fits September 2014 (it was 5.9% that month). The fed funds rate is 0.09% and the 10-year yield is 2.32%, with the 2-year at 0.48%. The dollar has strengthened sharply, up 4.18 points over three months. Gold has fallen 11.8% over 12 months, and developed ex-US equity is down 3.7% over 3 months, both consistent with that period.

The 10-year yield was about 2.5% at the end of September 2014 and about 2.3% at the end of October 2014. The September payroll average was around 220k. October's unemployment rate was 5.8%, so the 5.9% reading points to September, but October's data would have been the latest published only after the month-end release. At the end of October, the published unemployment rate would be September's 5.9%, since the October figure came out in early November.

US large-cap equity returned +3.7% in the month, which matches October 2014 (the S&P rose about 2.4%, so it is not a perfect match). The VIX at 14.5 is also consistent with the end of October 2014. The 3-month change in the 10-year yield of -0.26 fits too, since it was about 2.58% at the end of July. Headline CPI of 1.66% fits September 2014 (1.7%), and the 3-month change in the dollar fits as well.

I estimate October 2014.
